# Phobos Manufacturing: equipment and item reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/update-item-reference.ps1. Edit config/item-reference.json, not this file. -->

Current source candidate: **0.35.0**. Game target: **1.0.1.5**. Values below come from offline definitions; they do not establish installation, gameplay validation or a live merchant quote.

Phobos Manufacturing refines what the crew mines and runs the first chemistry aboard: the Fennmark V4 Volatiles Refinery, the X2 Chemical Processor (water electrolysis), the K2 Sabatier Reactor, the Tolvane AX-2 Ammonia Cracker, the Lixivar LC-3 Leach and Crystallise Unit and SA-3 Sulfuric Acid Plant, hydrogen, methane, oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide and ammonia stores and Lixivar sulfuric acid tanks in three sizes each, the P1 RCS Propellant Manifold, the L2 Canister Filling Station and the A2 Cabin Air Regulator, with nickel-iron ingots and carbon stock as raw stock, the LC-3's fertiliser salts and intermediates, the SA-3's phosphoric acid flask, eight terminal remainders and four minable chunks. Every charge conserves mass and is recorded with its chemistry and sources in [the refinery design record](development/manufacturing-refinery-and-chemistry.md); operating instructions are in [the player guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md). Machines are purchase-only; ores and chunks are mined, never bought; bulk oxygen, nitrogen and carbon dioxide are sold only through the station Bulk supplies view. The machines are late-game plant, priced among the game's own radars, heavy lift rotors and missile launchers; they carry the game's high-salvage mark, need component repairs and are rare world finds. See [the equipment economy](equipment-economy.md#manufacturing-011-late-game-plant).

**Reading prices:** credits per complete object at the stated condition, before shop margins, market effects, negotiation and extra wear. Pristine retail can cost more. Mass is the empty/dry definition or fresh commodity template; saved contents and variable recovery packets can weigh differently. Dismantle value is the sum of all listed outputs at base value, excluding labour and tools.

**Repair and Restore:** Repair fixes a damaged form and uses up its parts, as the game's own repairs do. Restore reduces wear on functional equipment in place; it does not grant pristine status. Empty cargo and follow the machine’s local maintenance guards first. Work speed depends on crew, tools and current condition.

**Finding stock:** the generated percentages are defaults per eligible native stock/loot roll, not per ship or guaranteed shop availability. Offers are additive, may be independent, and require normal restocking. Merchant offers request the listed finite lot when successful; separate world-loot branches retain their own listed quantities. Configuration, capacity and native generation rules still apply; loading an existing save does not refill its inventories.

**Stacking:** limits below apply to loose items on the ground or in compatible containers; 1 means no multi-item stack. Installed equipment remains individual. Limits count objects, not kilograms, and do not change merchant lot sizes or per-object contents.

## V4 Volatiles Refinery

A 4 x 4 electric hearth and drying retort. One charge at a time: hydrates (10 kg) to 1 kg of water and three gangue; clay hydrates to 2 kg of water and an 8 kg anhydrous residue; an ammonium salt crust to 0.955 kg of ammonia for a linked ammonia store, 0.505 kg of water, 1.235 kg of CO2 into the room and a spent salt cake; carbon ore to five carbon stock, 1 kg of water, one gangue and 1 kg of CO2, CO and smoke breathed into the room; meteoric iron to four nickel-iron ingots, one gangue and 1 kg of slag; an LC-3 leached residue (6.8 kg) to 0.26 kg of carbon dioxide for a linked carbon dioxide store and a 6.54 kg calcined residue; with Shipbreaker, four nickel-iron ingots and one carbon stock to four steel ingots and a melt remainder.

**Use:** Install through APPS, connect power, link a water vessel (S3 or R3 within one tile) on its panel or C1 for the water charges an ammonia store within one tile for the salt crust and a carbon dioxide store within one tile for a leached residue, load one charge into its feed (the Inventory opens the tray and the feed), then Start. 24 kW while working; part of it warms the room. Run a scrubber in its room for the carbon and salt crust charges. See [the player guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Fennmark machine, usually broken; see the exact offers below. The K-Leg fixer buys it back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Trusted standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

A melt (nickel-iron or steel) left waiting for a cool room longer than its own run freezes into slag. Reload pauses it; Start resumes the bound charge. A steel charge saved before Shipbreaker is removed is kept, never overwritten. Empty the tray by hand.

Full operating instructions: [V4 Volatiles Refinery guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

## X2 Chemical Processor

A 2 x 2 water electrolysis cell. Each one-hour cycle at 6 kW splits 1.125 kg of water into 1.000 kg of oxygen and 0.125 kg of hydrogen (2 H2O to 2 H2 + O2).

**Use:** Install through APPS within one tile of a water vessel and an H2 store, connect power, link both on its panel or C1, choose an installed O2 canister within one tile (or leave it on cabin air), then Start. It runs only while every output has room; a full canister or store makes it wait.

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Fennmark machine, usually broken; see the exact offers below. The K-Leg fixer buys it back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Trusted standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Oxygen into the cabin raises the oxygen partial pressure, which raises the game's own fire chance. Reload pauses it; Start resumes with the held water and cycle energy kept. Cancel forfeits the cycle's energy, never the water.

Full operating instructions: [X2 Chemical Processor guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

## H2, H3 and H4 Hydrogen Stores

Passive pressurised stores for electrolysis hydrogen (24, 59 and 115 kg), kept as a kilogram record (hydrogen has no game gas). Three sizes: small 2 x 2, medium 3 x 3 and large 4 x 4, each one tile wider and holding more for less per kilogram.

**Use:** Install through APPS within one tile of an X2 or an AX-2 ammonia cracker (which fill it) and, for the Sabatier stage, a K2 (which draws from it); link them from those machines. Vent overboard or pour into another store of the same gas (within one tile or along a gas line) from its panel or C1. Repair damage at once and empty it before uninstalling. It can also feed the RCS through a P1 manifold (within one tile or by gas line; switched off until you turn it on).

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices, and the bigger sizes cost less per kilogram held. No fabrication recipe. The small size is a rare engineering-loot find, usually broken; the medium and large sizes are too big to turn up in salvage. The K-Leg fixer buys them back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Damaged, a store leaks to space (about 2, 3 or 4 kg an hour by size) until repaired. With oxygen in the room and a fire, a working V4 hearth or a sparking damaged device, its contents burn: the room loses oxygen and warms, and the game's own explosion follows. Dismantling refuses while it holds hydrogen.

Full operating instructions: [H2, H3 and H4 Hydrogen Stores guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

## K2 Sabatier Reactor

A 2 x 2 catalytic Sabatier reactor, CO2 + 4 H2 -> CH4 + 2 H2O. Each one-hour cycle at 1.2 kW takes 0.125 kg of hydrogen (one X2 cycle) and 0.682 kg of CO2 and makes 0.559 kg of water and 0.249 kg of methane. The reaction and its electricity put about 2.3 kW into the room.

**Use:** Install through APPS within one tile of an H2 store, an installed native CO2 canister, a water vessel (S3 or R3) and an M2 methane store; connect power; link all four on its panel or C1; Start. Fill the CO2 canister with the game's CO2 scrubber. It waits, with the reason, while an input is short or an output full, and starts a new cycle only once the last cycle's products are delivered.

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Fennmark machine, usually broken; see the exact offers below. The K-Leg fixer buys it back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Trusted standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

With the X2 it returns about half the water the X2 splits, as NASA's ISS system does. Damaged, it dumps the gas it holds: CO2 and methane into the room, and its hydrogen burns if the room has oxygen and a spark, otherwise it escapes; water stays in its hold. Reload pauses it until Start. Dismantling refuses while it holds gas, water or a part-run cycle.

Full operating instructions: [K2 Sabatier Reactor guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

## AX-2 Ammonia Cracker

A 2 x 2 catalytic ammonia cracker from Tolvane, a new brand for the nitrogen line: each one-hour cycle at 2 kW splits 1 kg of ammonia into 0.822 kg of nitrogen and 0.178 kg of hydrogen (2 NH3 -> N2 + 3 H2).

**Use:** Install through APPS within one tile of an ammonia store, a nitrogen store and a hydrogen store (any sizes), connect power, set Ammonia from, Nitrogen to and Hydrogen to on its panel or C1, then Start. It works only when both product stores have room for a whole cycle. About 1.25 kW warms the room while it works. See [the player guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Manufacturing machine, usually broken; see the exact offers below. The K-Leg fixer buys it back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Trusted standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Reload pauses it; Start resumes. A damaged or destroyed cracker releases the ammonia and nitrogen it holds into the room and its hydrogen burns or escapes; it holds at most one cycle. Complete conversion is an authored simplification.

Full operating instructions: [AX-2 Ammonia Cracker guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

<a id="lc3"></a>

## LC-3 Leach and Crystallise Unit

A 3 x 3 leach tank and closed crystalliser from Lixivar, a new brand for hydrometallurgy. The crew chooses one of six recipes at 12 kW: an evaporite crust in 20 kg of circulating water to 0.70 kg of potassium sulfate, 0.25 kg of phosphate concentrate, a 6.8 kg leached residue and a 2.25 kg brine salt cake (one hour; the water comes back); a phosphate concentrate with 30 g of ammonia and 0.22 kg of water to 0.43 kg of struvite and 70 g of caustic remainder (five minutes); with Phobos Agriculture, one potassium sulfate and two struvite to 39 Groundwork makeup salts packets (two and a half minutes); one of the game's olivine chunks with 8.64 kg of sulfuric acid and 9.52 kg of water to 32 Epsom salt and a 14.33 kg olivine leach cake (one hour, about 5.3 kWh of reaction heat into the room); one phosphoric acid flask and three Epsom salt with 0.27 kg of ammonia to three struvite, three ammonium sulfate and 94 g of water back to the vessel (ten minutes); and, with Agriculture 0.27.0 or newer, one each of potassium sulfate, struvite, Epsom salt and ammonium sulfate with 0.25 kg of ammonia and 0.73 kg of acid to 2.77 kg of crop nutrients in a linked nutrient hopper (five minutes).

**Use:** Install through APPS within one tile of a water vessel (S3 or R3) and, as the recipes need them, an ammonia store, an acid tank and a Groundwork nutrient hopper; connect power; on its panel or C1 link them and choose the recipe; load that recipe's charge into its feed (the Inventory opens the tray and the feed), then Start. It works the next charge of the same recipe when one is in the feed. Change the recipe only while no charge is bound. See [the player guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Manufacturing machine, usually broken; see the exact offers below. The K-Leg fixer buys it back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Trusted standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Reload pauses it; Start resumes the bound charge. Nothing melts or spoils in it, and it breathes nothing into the room; 15 percent of its electricity warms the room. The crust's and the olivine's make-up, the Epsom yield, the blend's nitrogen level and the recipes' energies are authored; the reactions and sources are in the refinery design record. Empty the tray by hand.

Full operating instructions: [LC-3 Leach and Crystallise Unit guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

## SA-3 Sulfuric Acid Plant

A 3 x 3 roaster, converter bed and absorption tower from Lixivar. Each one-hour charge at 4 kW roasts one sulfide nodule in 6.28 kg of oxygen with 1.58 kg of water into 7.81 kg of sulfuric acid for a linked acid tank, a 0.515 kg phosphoric acid flask and 9.535 kg of roasted calcine. The reactions release about 21 kWh a nodule into the room.

**Use:** Install through APPS within one tile of an oxygen store, a water vessel and an acid tank; connect power; link all three on its panel or C1; load nodules into its feed (it holds two), then Start. Give it a large, cooled room: it waits whenever the room would pass 40 C. See [the player guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Manufacturing machine, usually broken; see the exact offers below. The K-Leg fixer buys it back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Trusted standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Reload pauses it; Start resumes the bound charge. It breathes nothing into the room, but its heat is real and, like every Phobos machine, it does not work in vacuum. The nodule's make-up and the plant's energy are authored; the reactions and sources are in the refinery design record.

Full operating instructions: [SA-3 Sulfuric Acid Plant guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

## M2, M3 and M4 Methane Stores

Passive pressurised stores for Sabatier methane (160, 395 and 770 kg), kept as a kilogram record, and a source of RCS propellant. Three sizes: small 2 x 2, medium 3 x 3 and large 4 x 4, each one tile wider and holding more for less per kilogram.

**Use:** Install through APPS within one tile of a K2 and link it from the reactor. Vent overboard or pour into another store of the same gas (within one tile or along a gas line) from its panel or C1. Repair damage at once and empty it before uninstalling. It feeds the RCS through a P1 manifold (within one tile or by gas line; switched off until you turn it on).

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices, and the bigger sizes cost less per kilogram held. No fabrication recipe. The small size is a rare engineering-loot find, usually broken; the medium and large sizes are too big to turn up in salvage. The K-Leg fixer buys them back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Methane is one of the game's own gases: a damaged store leaks about 2, 3 or 4 kg an hour into the room (to space where there is no air) until repaired, and a destroyed one releases what it held. With oxygen in the room and a fire, a working V4 hearth or a sparking damaged device, its contents burn, using 4 kg of oxygen and leaving 2.7 kg of CO2 per kg of methane, with the game's own explosion. Dismantling refuses while it holds methane.

Full operating instructions: [M2, M3 and M4 Methane Stores guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

## O2, O3 and O4 Oxygen Stores

Passive pressurised stores for bulk oxygen (340, 840 and 1,630 kg), kept as a kilogram record. Three sizes: small 2 x 2, medium 3 x 3 and large 4 x 4, each one tile wider and holding more for less per kilogram.

**Use:** Install through APPS. Fill it from an X2 (choose the store as the cell's oxygen destination) or buy bulk oxygen at a station's Bulk supplies. It feeds an L2 filling station, which tops up canisters and suit bottles, and the RCS through a P1 manifold. Vent overboard or pour into another store of the same gas (within one tile or along a gas line) from its panel or C1. Repair damage at once and empty it before uninstalling. 

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices, and the bigger sizes cost less per kilogram held. No fabrication recipe. The small size is a rare engineering-loot find, usually broken; the medium and large sizes are too big to turn up in salvage. The K-Leg fixer buys them back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Oxygen is one of the game's own gases: a damaged store leaks about 2, 3 or 4 kg an hour into the room until repaired, and a destroyed one releases what it held. Oxygen-rich air makes any fire worse. Bought oxygen costs the refuelling kiosk's own price per kilogram, and the kiosk buys stored oxygen back at 45% of it.

Full operating instructions: [O2, O3 and O4 Oxygen Stores guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

## N2, N3 and N4 Nitrogen Stores

Passive pressurised stores for bulk nitrogen (300, 745 and 1,440 kg), kept as a kilogram record. Three sizes: small 2 x 2, medium 3 x 3 and large 4 x 4, each one tile wider and holding more for less per kilogram.

**Use:** Install through APPS and buy bulk nitrogen at a station's Bulk supplies, or fill it from an AX-2 ammonia cracker within one tile. It feeds an L2 filling station, which refills RCS and air-pump canisters far from port, and the RCS directly through a P1 manifold. Vent overboard or pour into another store of the same gas (within one tile or along a gas line) from its panel or C1. Repair damage at once and empty it before uninstalling. 

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices, and the bigger sizes cost less per kilogram held. No fabrication recipe. The small size is a rare engineering-loot find, usually broken; the medium and large sizes are too big to turn up in salvage. The K-Leg fixer buys them back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Nitrogen is one of the game's own gases: a damaged store leaks about 2, 3 or 4 kg an hour into the room until repaired, thinning the air without warning, and a destroyed one releases what it held. Bought nitrogen costs the refuelling kiosk's own price per kilogram, and the kiosk buys stored nitrogen back at 45% of it.

Full operating instructions: [N2, N3 and N4 Nitrogen Stores guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

## Q2, Q3 and Q4 Ammonia Stores

Passive pressurised stores for liquefied ammonia (380, 940 and 1,820 kg), kept as a kilogram record. Three sizes: small 2 x 2, medium 3 x 3 and large 4 x 4, each one tile wider and holding more for less per kilogram.

**Use:** Install through APPS within one tile of a V4 and choose it under the refinery's Send ammonia to; the salt crust charge will not start without one. An AX-2 cracker splits it into nitrogen and hydrogen, or the RCS can burn it through a P1 manifold, at about 1.41 times nitrogen's push per kilogram. Vent overboard or pour into another ammonia store (within one tile or along a gas line) from its panel or C1. Repair damage at once and empty it before uninstalling. 

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices, and the bigger sizes cost less per kilogram held. No fabrication recipe. The small size is a rare engineering-loot find, usually broken; the medium and large sizes are too big to turn up in salvage. The K-Leg fixer buys them back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Ammonia is one of the game's own gases and poisons the crew: a damaged store leaks about 2, 3 or 4 kg an hour into the room until repaired, and a destroyed one releases what it held. Stations do not sell ammonia; it comes only from the salt crust. The refuelling kiosk buys stored ammonia at 45% of the game's ammonia price.

Full operating instructions: [Q2, Q3 and Q4 Ammonia Stores guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

<a id="acid-tanks"></a>

## AT-2, AT-3 and AT-4 Sulfuric Acid Tanks

Bunded tanks for concentrated sulfuric acid, kept as a kilogram record: 1,150 kg in the 2 x 2 AT-2, 2,850 kg in the 3 x 3 AT-3 and 5,520 kg in the 4 x 4 AT-4. Liquid tanks, not gas stores: no gas line and no feed to thrusters, filling stations or cabin air.

**Use:** Install through APPS touching an SA-3 (which fills it) or an LC-3 (which draws from it), or join them with acid line laid under or right beside both; link it from those machines. Buy acid into it at a station's Bulk supplies. Pour acid into another tank it touches or shares an acid line with, from its panel or C1. Empty it before moving or dismantling it. Since Manufacturing 0.25.0 each tank has a four-place rack for Framework drain canisters: a canister of acid put in it pours into the tank.

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices, and the bigger sizes cost less per kilogram held. No fabrication recipe. The small size is a rare engineering-loot find, usually broken; the medium and large sizes are too big to turn up in salvage. The K-Leg fixer buys them back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Damaged, the bund holds the acid but a ten-thousandth of it reaches the room as the game's own sulfuric acid mist, which poisons in its bands; repair, then recover the acid. A destroyed tank mists the same share and the rest is lost. A wet acid line that is damaged spills about a kilogram from the tank feeding it into this bund. Bought acid costs the game's own 3.1 cr/kg, and the kiosk buys stored acid back at 45% of it.

Full operating instructions: [AT-2, AT-3 and AT-4 Sulfuric Acid Tanks guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

<a id="acid-line"></a>

## Lixivar acid line

Lined line for concentrated sulfuric acid between the AT acid tanks and the machines that fill or draw from them: the SA-3 and the LC-3. Every acid tank, SA-3 and LC-3 the line runs under or right beside joins one network, and touching equipment joins without it. It has its own violet lane, so it shares tiles with other lines.

**Use:** Lay it through INSTALL > HVAC on intact floor until it runs under or right beside each machine and tank, on any side. Then link the machine to the tank on its Control Panel; the list shows how each tank is reached. To take it up, right-click it and choose Drain line into canister with a Framework drain canister carried or within two tiles; the run closes until Return line to service.

**Where it appears:** Sold new at the K-Leg supply kiosk and fixer, San Diego Halvorson and the Venus scrap kiosk in lots of 128. Ordinary supply. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks, at any standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → HVAC. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

New in Manufacturing 0.24.0. Since Manufacturing 0.25.0 it holds about 0.9 kg of acid a tile, filled from its tanks (an authored metre of 25 mm bore), and a segment holding acid cannot be taken up until drained. Damaged or destroyed, a segment lets a ten-thousandth of what it holds into the room as mist; a damaged one keeps the rest until drained. Dismantling returns only retained waste, which is terminal.

Full operating instructions: [Lixivar acid line guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

<a id="l2"></a>

## L2 Canister Filling Station

A powered 2 x 2 booster that tops up standard O2, N2 and CO2 canisters and suit O2 bottles to a safe 99% of their rated pressure and stops, even at fast-forward. Decant mode empties them back into bulk stores.

**Use:** Install through INSTALL > HVAC and power it from conduit. Put suit O2 bottles in its rack (Inventory), link canisters installed beside it, and link oxygen, nitrogen or carbon dioxide stores within one tile or along a gas line, switching each on. A linked canister can be set to Draw from it instead. Choose Fill or Decant, then press Start. After a reload it waits for Start. Right-click Keep suit bottles charged to have crew with the Haul duty bring loose bottles below 90% into the rack and start it; choose a destination store in the Crew panel for charged bottles.

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Fennmark machine, usually broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → HVAC. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Draws 3 kW while working; the electricity pays for compressing the gas (about 0.06 kWh per kilogram of oxygen into a canister) and all of it ends as heat in the room. Hydrogen and methane cannot be bottled: the game has no canister for them.

Full operating instructions: [L2 Canister Filling Station guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

<a id="a2"></a>

## A2 Cabin Air Regulator

A powered 2 x 2 valve and sensor unit that holds the room it stands in at an oxygen set point from a linked oxygen store, then at a pressure set point from a linked nitrogen store. It only adds gas.

**Use:** Install through INSTALL > HVAC in the room to look after and power it from conduit. Link an oxygen store and, for pressure, a nitrogen store within one tile or along a gas line, choose the set points and press Switch on. It keeps working after a reload.

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Fennmark machine, usually broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → HVAC. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Up to 6 kg of oxygen and 12 kg of nitrogen an hour. It stops feeding a room below 10 kPa (open to space) and never lets oxygen pass 30% of the air. It never vents, scrubs carbon dioxide or cools: keep the scrubbers running.

Full operating instructions: [A2 Cabin Air Regulator guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

## P1 RCS Propellant Manifold

A passive 1 x 1 valve block that feeds the ship's RCS thrusters from Fennmark gas stores (hydrogen, methane, oxygen, nitrogen or carbon dioxide). Each gas pushes by its own worth: methane about 1.45 times nitrogen per kilogram, hydrogen about 3.7 times.

**Use:** Install through INSTALL > HVAC on an RCS Intake Regulator's gas-input tile, where a gas canister would go. Link up to four stores within one tile, or along a gas line that runs under or right beside both, switch each on, choose Manifold first or Canisters first, and switch the manifold on. Everything starts off.

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Fennmark machine, usually broken; see the exact offers below. The K-Leg fixer buys it back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → HVAC. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Not a gas canister: station refuelling never fills it. Draws settle to the stores every couple of seconds and before a save. Auto Nav's fuel and delta-v readings count the stores in nitrogen-equivalent kilograms.

Full operating instructions: [P1 RCS Propellant Manifold guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

<a id="stock"></a>

## Raw stock, nickel steel and carbon black

Nickel-iron ingots (4 kg, cast meteoric iron: iron with a few percent of nickel), carbon stock (1 kg) and nickel steel ingots (4 kg) are the refinery's products. Four nickel-iron ingots with one carbon stock become four nickel steel ingots in the V4, with or without Shipbreaker; the coming machining centre consumes ingots. Carbon black (1 kg, Manufacturing 0.27.0) is cracked out of methane on a carbon stock bed, with hydrogen as the by-product; the V4 burns it with stored oxygen into carbon dioxide for grow rooms.

**Use:** Made in the V4. Carry, stack (ten per stack) and sell at any general buyer, or feed four nickel-iron ingots and one carbon stock back into the V4 for nickel steel. With a methane store and a hydrogen store linked to the V4, one carbon stock alone is a methane-cracking charge; with an oxygen store and a carbon dioxide store linked, one carbon black is a burning charge.

**Where it appears:** Made in the V4 from meteoric iron and carbon ore. Never sold in shops.

**Placement:** Inventory/module-slot item; no standalone INSTALL entry.

Refining pays (owner decision, 1 October 2026): four nickel-iron ingots ($880) are worth about twice the $450 meteoric iron block, five carbon stock ($190) with its water about twice the $99 carbon ore, and four nickel steel ingots ($1,040) about 2.2 times the iron and carbon ore behind them. Nickel steel is not Shipbreaker's plain steel ingot ($25), which the F6 casts from scrap. Ingots and carbon already aboard take the new prices when a save loads. Scrap kiosks do not buy them, so they are never furnace or processor feed. Carbon black is worth 12 cr, kept low so methane made from bought water and carbon dioxide never pays its way back as soot.

Full operating instructions: [Raw stock, nickel steel and carbon black guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

<a id="lixivar-salts"></a>

## Fertiliser salts and intermediates

Potassium sulfate (0.70 kg), struvite (0.43 kg, slow-release magnesium ammonium phosphate), Epsom salt (0.432 kg of magnesium sulfate from olivine) and ammonium sulfate (0.232 kg, from the acid-route struvite) are fertiliser salts; phosphate concentrate (0.25 kg) is struvite's feed; a leached residue (6.8 kg of washed clay and magnesium carbonate) is the V4's calcine feed.

**Use:** Made in the LC-3. Put a phosphate concentrate back in the LC-3 for struvite, or a phosphoric acid flask with three Epsom salt for struvite and ammonium sulfate; blend one potassium sulfate with two struvite for Groundwork makeup salts, or one of each of the four salts into crop nutrients for a nutrient hopper (with Agriculture); calcine a leached residue in the V4 for carbon dioxide. Sell the salts at any general buyer.

**Where it appears:** Made in the LC-3 from mined evaporite crust, the game's olivine and the SA-3's phosphoric acid. Never sold in shops.

**Placement:** Inventory/module-slot item; no standalone INSTALL entry.

Refining pays (owner decision, 1 October 2026): potassium sulfate 190 cr, phosphate concentrate 110 cr, struvite 125 cr, Epsom salt 13 cr and ammonium sulfate 20 cr, so leaching a crust earns about twice the crust and an olivine about 2.3 times the ore; the leached residue is priced as trash because the V4 takes it. The makeup salts are worth Agriculture's own 30 cr a packet, and crop nutrients its 1,500 cr/kg (bag a hopper's nutrients into bulk charges to sell them; the station does not buy them back from a hopper). Salts already aboard take the new prices when a save loads.

Full operating instructions: [Fertiliser salts and intermediates guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

## Terminal remainders

Refinery slag (1 kg: sulfide, phosphide and oxide skimmings, or a frozen melt), anhydrous residue (8 kg of baked clay minerals), spent salt cake (7.305 kg of table salt baked into clay), brine salt cake (2.25 kg of the evaporite crust's sodium salts), caustic remainder (70 g of sodium hydroxide from struvite), calcined residue (6.54 kg of baked clay and magnesia), roasted calcine (9.535 kg of iron and nickel oxides and rock from the SA-3), olivine leach cake (14.33 kg of silica gel, iron sulfate, rock and Epsom liquor from the LC-3) and exhausted sorbent (2.5 kg: the one CO2 filter in four that reactivation in the V4 cannot bring back). **Where it appears:** Left in the V4, LC-3 or SA-3 tray by their charges. Never sold.

**Placement:** Inventory/module-slot item; no standalone INSTALL entry.

Terminal: never re-processed, never the game's own Trash item.

## Ammonium salt crust

A 10 kg chunk of pale salt crust: ammonium chloride with sodium carbonate and clay, like the bright salt deposits NASA's Dawn mission found on Ceres. The ship's only mined source of nitrogen.

**Use:** Bake it in the V4 with an ammonia store linked: 0.955 kg of ammonia to the store, 0.505 kg of water to the linked vessel, 1.235 kg of carbon dioxide into the room and a 7.305 kg spent salt cake in the tray. Or sell it to a government kiosk like other ore.

**Where it appears:** Mined: C-class deposits and dark regolith walls turn it up in place of some of the silicates they would otherwise give: about one pull in twenty-one from a C-class deposit, far fewer from walls. Never sold.

**Placement:** Inventory/module-slot item; no standalone INSTALL entry.

The mix (30 percent ammonium chloride) is authored from the Dawn findings; see the chemistry record for sources and the rounding.

<a id="evaporite-crust"></a>

## Evaporite crust

A 10 kg chunk of salt-streaked clay from a dried brine vein: rock salt, potassium chloride, sodium sulfate and carbonate, a little magnesium phosphate and a trace of fluoride salt, the minerals NASA's OSIRIS-REx team reported in samples from the asteroid Bennu.

**Use:** Leach it in the LC-3 for potassium sulfate, phosphate concentrate, a leached residue and a brine salt cake, or sell it to a government kiosk like other ore.

**Where it appears:** Mined: C-class deposits and dark regolith walls turn it up in place of some of the silicates they would otherwise give: about one pull in twenty-one from a C-class deposit, far fewer from walls. Never sold.

**Placement:** Inventory/module-slot item; no standalone INSTALL entry.

The minerals follow McCoy et al. 2025 (Nature); the paper gives no bulk fractions, so the proportions (0.60 kg of potassium chloride per chunk, for example) are authored. See the chemistry record for sources and the rounding.

Full operating instructions: [Evaporite crust guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

<a id="sulfide-nodule"></a>

## Sulfide nodule

A 10 kg chunk of troilite (iron sulfide) with schreibersite, a nickel-iron phosphide, of the kind found in iron meteorites. The ship's source of sulfur and phosphorus.

**Use:** Roast it in an SA-3 for sulfuric acid and a phosphoric acid flask, or sell it to a government kiosk like other ore.

**Where it appears:** Mined: M-class and S-class deposits turn it up in place of some of their meteoric iron, about one pull in thirty-six from an M-class deposit and one in sixty-three from an S-class one. Never sold.

**Placement:** Inventory/module-slot item; no standalone INSTALL entry.

The mix (7.000 kg troilite, 1.058 kg phosphide, 1.942 kg rock) is authored after Buchwald's handbook of iron meteorites; see the chemistry record.

Full operating instructions: [Sulfide nodule guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

<a id="compartments"></a>

## Built-in charge feeds

The V4's, the LC-3's and the SA-3's charge feeds, named child inventories built into the machines. Not separate products.

**Use:** Open one from its machine's Inventory. The V4 takes single ore blocks, clay chunks, salt crusts, leached residues, nickel-iron ingots or carbon stock; the LC-3 takes only the chosen recipe's feed (an evaporite crust, a phosphate concentrate, or potassium sulfate and struvite). The SA-3 takes sulfide nodules only. Each binds one exact charge at a time.

**Where it appears:** Shown as feed inventory within the V4, the LC-3 or the SA-3.

**Placement:** Built into its parent machine; not separately installable.

No purchase, INSTALL, repair, Restore or standalone salvage contract.

Full operating instructions: [Built-in charge feeds guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

Included compartments: Phobos' Fennmark V4 Refinery charge; Phobos' Lixivar LC-3 Leach unit charge; Phobos' Lixivar SA-3 Acid plant charge.

<a id="deflagration"></a>

## Gas deflagration

The game's own explosion objects in three sizes, spawned for a moment when a damaged or destroyed fuel store (hydrogen or methane) or a damaged reactor's hydrogen burns. Not items.

**Use:** Not usable. They apply the game's radius damage, shrapnel and fire rolls and remove themselves.

**Where it appears:** Only where stored fuel burns.

**Placement:** Built into its parent machine; not separately installable.

Their entries live in the mod's data/explosions file.

Full operating instructions: [Gas deflagration guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

Included compartments: Gas deflagration; Gas deflagration; Gas deflagration.

## Evidence and upkeep

Item names, dry/template masses, prices, service bills, salvage outputs, placement tabs, stock probabilities and table recipes are generated from current Phobos definitions. **Blue Bottle Games’ Ostranauts** native `DataCO.GetBasePrice` supplies the offline valuation used here ([developer’s game page](https://bluebottlegames.com/games/ostranauts)). That page identifies the game; the actual numeric evidence is the locally inspected assembly, whose hash is retained in the generated data snapshot. No proprietary source or game assembly is distributed.

Function/use explanations are maintained in the reviewed catalogue. All fictional prices, yields and simplified processing are Phobos gameplay choices. Research attribution remains beside the relevant claims in the linked operating/research guides. See [reference maintenance](development/item-reference-maintenance.md) for the one-click updater and coverage checks.
